units.name: Constitutional Framework
units.description: Introduces the meaning, importance, salient features, and sources of the Indian Constitution.

cards.heading: What this unit covers
cards.body: This unit explains the Constitution as the basic framework of government. It covers why a constitution is needed, why India adopted a written and detailed Constitution, and how constitutional supremacy works.
cards.tip: Use it as the foundation for all later Polity units.

cards.heading: Core themes
cards.body: The main themes are constitutionalism, written constitution, federalism with unitary bias, parliamentary government, independent judiciary, judicial review, democracy, republic, secularism, and borrowed features.

cards.heading: Exam relevance
cards.body: UPSC often frames this area through statement-based questions on features, sources, constitutional supremacy, and federal-unitary balance.
cards.tip: Expect conceptual traps, not only direct facts.

cards.heading: Constitution
cards.body: A Constitution is the basic law of a country. It creates institutions, distributes powers, protects rights, sets procedures, and limits State authority.

cards.heading: Constitutionalism
cards.body: Constitutionalism means limited government. Political power must be exercised through constitutional rules, procedures, values, and rights.
cards.tip: A country may have a constitution but weak constitutionalism.

cards.heading: Supreme law
cards.body: The Constitution is superior to ordinary law. Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws, but those laws must conform to the Constitution.
cards.tip: This is the basis for judicial review.

cards.heading: Written and detailed
cards.body: India has a written and detailed Constitution due to diversity, federal needs, administrative complexity, colonial legacy, and the goal of social transformation.

cards.heading: Federal with unitary bias
cards.body: India has federal features like written Constitution, division of powers, independent judiciary, and constitutional supremacy. But the Union is stronger in many areas.
cards.tip: This is a classic UPSC phrase.

cards.heading: Parliamentary government
cards.body: India follows a parliamentary system where the executive is responsible to the legislature. The President is the constitutional head, while the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers exercise real executive power.

cards.heading: Judicial review
cards.body: Judicial review allows courts to examine whether laws and executive actions conform to the Constitution.

cards.heading: Borrowed but adapted
cards.body: The Constitution borrowed many provisions from other systems but adapted them to Indian conditions.

lessons.name: What is a Constitution?
lessons.description: A constitution is the basic framework that creates government, distributes power, protects rights, and limits authority.

cards.heading: Lesson preview
cards.body: This lesson introduces what is a constitution? in the context of the Indian Constitution.
cards.tip: Read for concept first, then fact.

cards.heading: Main takeaway
cards.body: A constitution is the basic framework that creates government, distributes power, protects rights, and limits authority.
cards.tip: Convert this into one sentence before moving ahead.

cards.heading: Basic meaning
cards.body: A Constitution is a set of basic rules according to which a country is governed. It defines institutions, powers, procedures, rights, and limits.
cards.tip: It is the foundation of public authority.

cards.heading: Creates institutions
cards.body: The Constitution creates institutions such as legislature, executive, judiciary, and constitutional bodies.

cards.heading: Distributes power
cards.body: It distributes power among organs and levels of government to prevent concentration of authority.

cards.heading: Protects citizens
cards.body: It protects citizens through rights and remedies against unlawful or arbitrary State action.

cards.heading: Limits government
cards.body: Even elected governments must follow constitutional boundaries.

cards.heading: Quick revision
cards.body: What is a Constitution? is important because it explains a core feature of India's constitutional framework.
cards.tip: Revise the main idea, not just terms.

cards.heading: UPSC angle
cards.body: UPSC can test what is a constitution? through correct/incorrect statements and close constitutional traps.
cards.tip: Watch absolute words like only, always and never.

cards.heading: Module focus

cards.heading: Learning method
cards.body: For every feature, learn meaning, Indian form and UPSC trap.

cards.heading: Big idea
cards.body: The Indian Constitution balances federal and unitary, rigid and flexible, rights and restrictions, democracy and judicial review.

cards.heading: Written and detailed
cards.body: The Constitution covers institutions, rights, duties, Union-State relations, emergencies, elections, services, schedules and amendments.

cards.heading: Rigid and flexible
cards.body: Some provisions can be changed by simple majority, some by special majority and some by special majority plus state ratification.

cards.heading: Federal with unitary bias
cards.body: India has federal features but a stronger Union.

cards.heading: Parliamentary system
cards.body: The executive is responsible to the legislature, and real power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

cards.heading: Independent judiciary
cards.body: The judiciary protects the Constitution and rights through independence and judicial review.

cards.heading: Secular democratic republic
cards.body: India is democratic, republican and secular, each with a precise constitutional meaning.

modules.name: Sources of the Constitution
modules.description: Covers borrowed features, Government of India Act 1935 influence, and Indian adaptations.

cards.heading: Module focus
cards.body: This module explains where important features of the Constitution came from.

cards.heading: Main idea
cards.body: India borrowed from many systems but adapted each feature to Indian needs.

cards.heading: Major source
cards.body: The Government of India Act, 1935 strongly influenced administrative and federal features.

cards.heading: Borrowed features
cards.body: The Constitution borrowed features from the UK, USA, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan, South Africa and others.

cards.heading: UK influence
cards.body: Parliamentary government, rule of law, cabinet system, legislative procedure, writs and single citizenship are linked with Britain.

cards.heading: USA influence
cards.body: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of judiciary and impeachment of President are linked with the USA.

cards.heading: Ireland and Canada
cards.body: DPSPs are inspired by Ireland. Federation with strong Centre and residuary powers with Centre are linked with Canada.

cards.heading: Government of India Act 1935
cards.body: This Act influenced federal scheme, Governor, judiciary, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and administrative details.

cards.heading: Indian adaptation
cards.body: The framers modified borrowed features to suit Indian democracy, diversity, social justice and national unity.

recapQuestions.questionText: Parliamentary government is mainly inspired by:
recapQuestions.explanation: Parliamentary government is mainly from the UK.

recapQuestions.questionText: Fundamental Rights are mainly inspired by:
recapQuestions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are inspired by the USA.

recapQuestions.questionText: DPSPs are inspired by:
recapQuestions.explanation: DPSPs are inspired by Ireland.

recapQuestions.questionText: Residuary powers with Centre are linked with:
recapQuestions.explanation: Canada influenced this feature.

recapQuestions.questionText: The 1935 Act strongly influenced:
recapQuestions.explanation: It influenced structure and administration.

questions.explanation: This is associated with South Africa.
